newsitem.title: USA: New drug inspectors to check U.S.-Mexico bridges.
newsitem.headline: New drug inspectors to check U.S.-Mexico bridges.

text.p: The U.S. Customs Service will get dozens of new inspectors to help reduce drug trafficking by searching more vehicles as they cross bridges on the U.S.-Mexico border, officials said on Monday.
Drug seizures on international bridges in the border city of El Paso, a key crossing point for traffickers, have soared in the last 18 months but officials said more help was needed.

"We need more inspectors so we can do more searches for drugs and other contraband," said U.S. Customs spokesman Roger Maier. "We are constantly seeing an increase in the amount of drugs being smuggled across."

Thirty new inspectors were deployed on Monday and 41 more are expected to be sworn in during the next few months. The 71 new inspectors will bring the total number of inspectors working El Paso's bridges up to about 350.
The agency is also supposed to get 22 new canine teams of one handler and one dog. These teams should be in place in the next few months.
In the past 18 months, heroin seizures here have grown 108 percent, marijuana seizures are up 25 percent and cocaine seizures are also up about 20 percent, officials said .
